Hi Anna — great to meet you over email. Happy to run the demo the week of March 10–14. Quick note on DST: the US moves clocks forward on Sunday March 9, 2025, while most of Europe moves on Sunday March 30, 2025. That creates a 1-hour offset difference for meetings between Mar 9 and Mar 29.

To avoid confusion, here are two concrete options with timezone conversions (all times listed with local zones):

Option A — earlier window (EMEA-friendly)
- Wed Mar 12, 10:00–11:00 CET / Wed Mar 12, 05:00–06:00 ET / Wed Mar 12, 02:00–03:00 PT / Wed Mar 12, 17:00–18:00 HKT

Option B — later window (EMEA late afternoon)
- Thu Mar 13, 16:00–17:00 CET / Thu Mar 13, 11:00–12:00 ET / Thu Mar 13, 08:00–09:00 PT / Thu Mar 13, 23:00–00:00 HKT

Notes: 1) Because US DST lands on Mar 9, the ET/PT times above already reflect the US-forwarded clock (i.e., US local times shift before EU does). 2) To keep invites stable for attendees across regions, we'll create the calendar event in UTC and include explicit local-time conversions in the invite body; that prevents client-side DST re-interpretation.

I've attached a short pre-demo checklist and will follow up with internal coverage. Let me know which option works for you and I'll send a calendar invite (ICS) and a list of Redwood participants.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
